text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1% today to close at $131.83, continuing a sharp three-day slide that began after the stock jumped to $141.22 on September 15th. The immediate driver appears to be easing concerns over Middle East supply disruptions: Saudi Arabia has signaled it can route more crude through the Strait of Hormuz to compensate for pipeline damage, which calmed market fears of a prolonged shortage. That relief, combined with oil markets finishing the prior week flat despite regional tensions, has taken some of the urgency out of energy stocks.

The broader picture is more mixed. While the near-term geopolitical risk has moderated slightly, the region remains volatile—fires near Riyadh airport and ongoing Saudi-Houthi clashes mean disruption could flare up again quickly. Additionally, record diesel prices and persistent global oil pricing (Brent crude at $130.80 per barrel versus US crude at $107) suggest structural tightness in energy markets hasn't disappeared, only that this particular scare has eased for now.
